title: Causal goal-axis frame with joint action-relation diffusion
coverage_gap: D_2 does not show independent stick and goal variation or the extrapolated target directions. It also sparsely covers the transition from approaching a free tool to maintaining a grasped offset and moving the pushed object. Training an action-only denoiser in world coordinates need not discover either directional reuse or those coupled geometric constraints.
reusable_regularity: Express translation commands and relative geometry in a horizontal frame whose forward axis is the observed pushed-object-to-goal displacement at chunk start. Keep world vertical fixed. Use one fixed frame for the entire sixteen-action chunk, both whole observation histories and both native subframes. Simultaneously diffuse action4 and nine next-state relation coordinates (hand-stick, stick-pushed-object, pushed-object-goal). The joint distribution is a learned coupling of actions with contact/transport geometry, not a planner, trajectory lookup, deterministic controller or inference-time future-state conditioning.

dependencies_preserved.world_and_robot: The frame is an invertible coordinate choice, not an assertion of exact workspace rotational symmetry. Absolute current and previous hand anchors remain in world coordinates, frame cosine/sine is explicitly conditioned, and z is the native gravity axis. Fixed end-effector orientation and the world action cube remain relevant.
dependencies_preserved.objects: The chain plus hand anchors and frame recovers both native positions. Current/previous xyzw quaternions are transformed by the inverse frame yaw and retained, so tool/fixture orientation relative to the intended displacement is visible. Object2 uses the declared insertion-site-plus-offset observation and its all-zero quaternion stays an all-zero placeholder under rotation; no physical orientation is invented.
dependencies_preserved.goal: The complete goal relative vector, its frame direction and world anchor remain recoverable; no mean target or sampled factor label replaces it.
dependencies_preserved.obstacles: Both observed objects and their relative geometry remain available. No hidden body poses, contact forces, table collision queries, simulated paths or additional obstacle channels are introduced. The frame is not a collision-free path.
dependencies_preserved.history: Every rotation is derived from raw_current at chunk start. Previous poses are expressed in that same frame, not a changing frame that confounds velocity with frame motion. Native one-step displacement and aperture change are explicit.

evidence_refs.detail: Only the two current-support episodes and their provided images/trajectories are used.
World xyz displacement plus scalar gripper, fixed rotation, goal/object2 observation definitions and C/E factor directions.

Initial pushed-object-to-goal vectors approximately [0.1995,-0.0301,0] and [0.2001,-0.0146,0] define nearby but distinct horizontal directions. Pushed-object y has very little observed variation, cautioning against assuming exact yaw symmetry.

Read obs 20:35 and 43:51 and actions 25:45,45:57: hand-stick offset stabilizes during lift, then the positive-x action persists while approaching the second object. This motivates coupled relation/action modeling, not a direct hand-to-goal point model.
Read obs 22:27 and 43:48 show a similar raised hand-tool offset at different stick and target placements.
Actual inspected tabletop view with raised pushed assembly and nearby tool/robot.
Actual inspected lifted-tool stage near the assembly.
Actual inspected later interaction supports retaining both objects rather than treating only the stick as the goal object.
Actual inspected late second-demo frame; world fixture and robot constraints are not rotated by changing target_y.
Joint diffusion is permitted with encoded native action4 first; gripper is not a translation vector; native clipping remains outside the candidate.
Shared diffusion generator samples all joint channels at inference, action4 is decoded, and the fixed action epsilon loss remains separate from auxiliary epsilon loss.

expected_failure_signature: If the task is predominantly world-axis constrained, goal-axis generalization may be inappropriate: extrapolated target_y could induce unnecessary sideways tool commands, a missed fixture, or early grasp errors despite a correct forward push component. The exposed world frame and relative orientations allow, but do not guarantee, learning that correction. Joint relation diffusion may learn nominal contact geometry even when a grasp actually fails, causing confident transport without a tool. A further failure is increased denoising error/latency from nine auxiliary channels at the unchanged budget. No outcome is claimed.

required_runtime_fields.source: Only shared causal_context.raw_history [B,2,39] and raw_current [B,39]. No cached trajectory, episode ID, time index or future labels.
required_runtime_fields.condition: 54 physical-scale channels per observation: two 21-channel pose/relation/quaternion blocks, ten finite-difference channels and two chunk-frame horizontal direction components. Scales are fixed physical constants; no fitted statistics or learned external encoder.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Let (c,s)=normalize(goal_xy-object2_xy) at chunk start, falling back to world +x only below 1e-6 m. Encode (a_x,a_y,a_z,a_g) as (c*a_x+s*a_y,-s*a_x+c*a_y,a_z,a_g). Decode by the inverse horizontal rotation. No translations of displacement actions, scaling, per-step re-framing, sample clipping or gripper rotation occur. Only the host clips the decoded world action cube and executes four of sixteen. Local translations can legitimately exceed individual [-1,1] coordinates.

training_only_targets.name: future_relations_world
training_only_targets.source_fields: For each exact D_N window (episode,t) and each valid action j with t+j<T: next observation obs[t+j+1] provides stick_xyz-hand_xyz, object2_xyz-stick_xyz, goal_xyz-object2_xyz. Nine world-meter values are rotated into the causal chunk-start frame, not a future-derived frame, then scaled by grasp/tool/goal metric scales. Padded entries are zeros and excluded from loss.
training_only_targets.joint_layout: Channels 0:4 are exactly encoded native action4. Channels 4:7 are next hand-to-stick relative coordinates, 7:10 next stick-to-pushed-object coordinates, 10:13 next pushed-object-to-goal coordinates. All are jointly noised by the shared scheduler. At deployment all thirteen channels start as host-generated noise; auxiliary channels are generated latent outcomes and discarded after sampling, never observations or a condition hook input.
training_only_targets.loss: Additional 0.25 times auxiliary epsilon squared error, normalized separately by 9 times sum(public action mask intersect relation_valid), with denominator floor 1 for empty masks. The fixed action epsilon loss retains weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4; no auxiliary error is added to its denominator or its channels.

change_summary: Initial independent scientific candidate: causal invertible action/observation yaw frame and a 13-channel common U-Net jointly diffusing actions and interaction relations. No learned motion-head or interaction gate, no support fitting, and no use of candidate performance. No structural repair before the initial check.
